taxonomy.note: Kew POWO and ITIS currently accept Celtis lindheimeri as a species, while USDA GRIN (verified 2026) treats it as a synonym of Celtis reticulata and notes that the type corresponds to the central Texas form of C. reticulata.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: NatureServe documents southeastern Bexar County as a known Texas occurrence. Broader sources describe central/southern Texas or Edwards Plateau presence, but B091 did not lock two additional exact target-zone counties under a stable taxonomic concept.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Need both a project taxonomy decision and at least two more exact target-zone counties if retained as a distinct species.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not silently merge into C. reticulata while Kew/ITIS still accept the species; do not count broad Balcones/Edwards Plateau range statements as county records.

morphology.look_here_first: Lindheimer hackberry is the white-under-leaf hackberry: lower leaf surfaces are densely white-tomentose, upper surfaces dark and rough, and mature fruits are usually light brown.
diagnostic_traits: upper leaf surface dark green and rough
margins entire or with few teeth
morphology.comparison_training: C. laevigata has smoother thinner foliage without the dense white tomentum beneath. C. reticulata has strongly raised netlike veins beneath but is not uniformly white-tomentose.

provisional_promotion.user_directive: Install for active learning now; correct later if field learning reveals errors.
